title: Embedded SDK
summary: A C99 library that firmware compiles in to be a Sparkplug B edge node: a gateway with devices behind it, or one direct device. The integrator registers device types, writes values and handles commands. The SDK owns the session (births, deaths, sequence numbers, aliases, rebirths) in one caller-allocated structure, without the heap, and reaches the hardware only through ports.

boxes.label: Firmware starter
boxes.sub: Generated by the API, no secrets
boxes.detail: A project for one target and one role (gateway or direct device), built from published profile revisions: the SDK, generated type tables, an AI brief and application stubs. Built targets are the ESP32, the NXP i.MX RT1050 and Linux; other families get an AI-assisted starter with porting notes.

boxes.label: Device type tables
boxes.detail: Each device type is a constant table of metrics (name, datatype, writable) that lives in flash. The SDK keeps no metric values. Defaults allow 8 types of up to 64 metrics and 512 devices; every limit is a compile-time setting that sizes the gateway structure.

boxes.label: Connection settings
boxes.detail: Broker host and port, group, edge node and host IDs, username, password and CA, for one gateway or direct device. A starter builds without them: until the settings file is added the program says where to get it and stops without connecting.

boxes.label: Integrator code
boxes.detail: The part a developer writes: one task that calls `iotos_poll` every 10 to 100 ms, and callbacks. `on_birth` fills current values, `on_command` applies a validated command and publishes the new state, `on_event` reports connection, clock and rejected commands.

boxes.label: iotos.h
boxes.detail: The whole public API: init, register types, start, poll, stop; add, remove or mark a device offline; open a writer, put values, commit. All state is in one `iotos_gateway` the caller allocates. Device and writer calls may come from any task and take the lock port.

boxes.label: Session
boxes.detail: Connects with a clean session and an NDEATH will carrying a bdSeq that goes up, and is saved, before every connection. It waits for the host application's STATE, then sends NBIRTH with seq 0 and the device births, 20 a second by default. Failed connections back off from 1 second to 5 minutes with jitter.

boxes.label: MQTT client
boxes.detail: Two port levels. Over a TLS byte stream the SDK runs MQTT 3.1.1 itself with the vendored coreMQTT. A modem that runs TLS and MQTT itself implements the MQTT port and hands received messages to `iotos_mqtt_inbound`.

boxes.label: Ports
boxes.sub: Stream or MQTT, clock, storage, lock
boxes.detail: The integrator's side. One of stream or MQTT, and a clock, are required. Storage keeps bdSeq across reboots, log and lock are optional. Ready sets exist for POSIX, ESP-IDF, and the MCUXpresso SDK with lwIP; FreeRTOS has a lock and a log; templates cover the rest.

boxes.label: Devices and writers
boxes.detail: A device slot is free, offline, waiting for its birth, or born. A commit for a device that is not born sends nothing and returns `IOTOS_PENDING_BIRTH`, because data before a birth would make the runtime ask the whole node for a rebirth. Each put is checked against the metric's datatype and range.

boxes.label: Codec
boxes.detail: Encodes straight into the 4 KiB transmit buffer and decodes commands from the 1 KiB receive buffer. Births carry every metric with name, alias and datatype; data carries the alias only. Its output is checked byte for byte against shared contract fixtures that the runtime replays.

boxes.label: Inbound
boxes.detail: Handles the three subscriptions. A rebirth request, or a second online STATE, queues every birth again. A command must name a born device and a writable metric with the declared datatype and a value in range; anything else, or one that arrives before this session's births, is rejected and reported through `on_event`. Retained commands are ignored.

boxes.label: Platform MQTT broker
boxes.detail: The SDK subscribes to exactly its own NCMD topic, DCMD for its devices and the host's STATE topic. The client ID is the username from the connection settings.

steps.text: A developer downloads a starter for a profile and a target. It contains the SDK and type tables generated from the profile, and no credentials.
The firmware initialises the gateway with its settings, ports and callbacks, registers its device types and adds the devices it serves.
`iotos_start` begins connecting, and one task then calls `iotos_poll` often. All network work, births and callbacks happen inside that call.
Before each connection the session raises bdSeq and saves it, then connects with an NDEATH will that carries it.
The bytes go through the integrator's ports: a verified TLS stream, or a modem that runs MQTT itself. Once connected the SDK subscribes to its commands and the host's STATE.
Nothing is published until the host application's retained STATE says it is online.
Then the session sends NBIRTH with seq 0 and one DBIRTH per device, paced, asking `on_birth` for current values. Births wait for a valid clock.
The application writes readings through a writer. A commit for a born device sends DDATA; for a device whose birth is still queued it sends nothing.
Data messages carry aliases instead of names, and every message after the NBIRTH takes the next sequence number, wrapping after 255.

A rebirth request from the runtime, or the host coming online again, sends every birth again. A valid command reaches `on_command`, which publishes the new value; that reading is what confirms the command.

When the connection drops, the session forgets its births and reconnects with a growing, jittered delay. Three connections closed within 10 seconds of opening, inside five minutes, are reported as another client using the same credentials.
